      <title>Clinical effects of mobile app (Keep)–based exercise management in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy</title>
      <scientificTitle>Clinical effects of mobile app (Keep)–based exercise management in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy: a nonrandomized, non-concurrent controlled quasiexperimental study</scientificTitle>
      <acronym/>
      <studyHypothesis>To evaluate the association between a 12-week mobile platform (Keep app)-supported exercise management program and neuropathy severity in patients with diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN). Secondary objectives include assessing the effects of the program on glycemic control, lower-extremity functional mobility, quality of life, and self-reported exercise adherence.</studyHypothesis>
      <plainEnglishSummary>Background and study aims
Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is a common complication of diabetes that affects the nerves, most often in the feet and legs. It can cause symptoms such as pain, numbness, tingling, weakness, and problems with balance and walking. Regular exercise may help reduce symptoms and improve health, but many people find it difficult to maintain an exercise programme on their own. This study aims to find out whether a mobile phone app called Keep can support people with diabetic peripheral neuropathy to follow a structured exercise programme and improve their nerve symptoms, blood sugar control, physical function, quality of life, and exercise habits.

Who can participate?
Adults aged 18 to 65 years with type 2 diabetes and mild to moderate diabetic peripheral neuropathy can take part. Participants must be using exercise infrequently, be able to use a smartphone, complete study questionnaires independently, and provide written informed consent.

What does the study involve?
A total of 72 participants take part in the study. Participants are enrolled into two groups at different times. One group receives usual care, which includes routine treatment, nursing care, health education about diet, exercise and medication monitoring, and weekly telephone follow-up calls.
The second group receives the same usual care plus a 12-week exercise management programme delivered through the Keep mobile app. The programme includes aerobic and resistance exercises performed three times per week, with each session lasting about 50 minutes. Participants also receive exercise guidance, daily reminders through WeChat, and weekly telephone calls from the research team. Exercise intensity is adjusted during the programme according to participants’ progress.
Researchers assess participants at the start of the study and again during and after the programme. They measure nerve symptoms, blood sugar levels, mobility, quality of life, and how closely participants follow their exercise programme.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Participants in the exercise programme may experience improvements in their nerve symptoms, physical function, blood sugar control, quality of life, and ability to maintain regular exercise. The information gained may also help improve future care for people with diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
As with any exercise programme, there is a possibility of discomfort, tiredness, muscle soreness, or minor exercise-related injuries. To reduce these risks, participants receive guidance and regular monitoring throughout the programme. People with medical conditions that could make exercise unsafe are not eligible to take part.

Where is the study run from?
The study is run from Hebei University of Chinese Medicine in Shijiazhuang, China. 

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
April 2025 to June 2026.

Who is funding the study?
The study is funded by the Social Science Fund of Hebei Province (Project No. HB23SH016). 

Who is the main contact?
Dr Huiling Feng
School of Nursing, Hebei University of Chinese Medicine, Shijiazhuang, China
Email: fenghuiling@hebcm.edu.cn</plainEnglishSummary>

      <title>A study of the REACTIVE app to monitor cognitive health in older adults</title>
      <scientificTitle>Clinical Investigation to determine the accuracy of cognitive monitoring and feedback app, REACTIVE, to detect and predict cognitive decline in older adults</scientificTitle>
      <acronym/>
      <studyHypothesis>To establish the sensitivity and specificity of the REACTIVE app to detect and predict clinically meaningful cognitive decline and conversion to dementia/MCI in adults at risk of dementia.</studyHypothesis>
      <plainEnglishSummary>Background and study aims
Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) affects about 10-20% of older adults, of whom 15% will develop dementia each year. Despite this, 99% of people with MCI are not in contact with healthcare services and wait until a crisis point before seeking help. There is currently no means of identifying these people in the community or any means of supporting them and their GP to manage their brain health and reduce their risk of dementia through evidence-based treatments. Computerised cognitive testing offers the potential for large-scale monitoring of cognition in the community. This would enable early detection, support and treatment of early cognitive impairment whilst driving efficiency and filling gaps in clinical pathways. REACTIVE is a combined technology that brings together cognitive monitoring and a digital platform with a track record for engagement of older adults. REACTIVE provides a user-friendly patient-facing app that can monitor brain health and identify people who are at risk of developing dementia. It can then alert primary care to trigger further assessment and diagnosis, thus providing a means of triaging patients into the dementia diagnostic pathway.

This study aims to establish the sensitivity and specificity of the REACTIVE app to detect and predict clinically meaningful cognitive decline and conversion to dementia/MCI in adults at risk of dementia.

Who can participate?
Adults aged 65 years and over with a current diagnosis of MCI or subjective concerns regarding their cognitive function.

What does the study involve?
This is a 30-month research study that will test the REACTIVE technology and see how well it performs when it is used by people at home. The study will recruit 1306 people over 65 who are experiencing concerns about their brain health. Of these, 628 participants will have MCI. They will download the app or use the REACTIVE website for 30 months, which will involve completing brain tests every six months. REACTIVE will identify people whose brain function suggests they may be developing dementia, and will use statistical tests and clinical review to check whether REACTIVE has correctly identified the right people. Participants will also provide saliva and blood samples through the post. The study team will analyse these samples to look for biological indicators of dementia risk. The saliva sample will be analysed to look for genes that are known to be linked to Alzheimer’s Disease and other causes of dementia. The blood sample will be analysed to look for proteins in the blood that are linked to changes in the brain. These indicators are still being confirmed by research and so the team cannot be certain that the information found will affect the participants’ chance of developing dementia. For this reason, the results of these tests will not be shared with participants.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
This study is aiming to improve how to detect the early symptoms of dementia in people who are not yet in touch with their GP about their brain health. By taking part in this study, it could help move forward our understanding of MCI and dementia and how it should be managed and supported. 

There is a small risk with providing a finger-prick blood sample. Most people experience mild discomfort when they complete these tests. Some people experience bruising or additional bleeding. Any more serious complications are extremely rare, but participant safety will be monitored during the study, and they will be able to report any safety concerns through the REACTIVE account or by contacting the study team.
This study does not replace NHS and if you feel less well during the time you are part of this study it is important that you seek help from your doctor or local health 

Where is the study run from?
The study is being led by the University of Exeter Medical School, in partnership with the Royal Devon University Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust and a network of NHS centres and GP practices.

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
November 2026 to September 2029.

Who is funding the study?
The National Institute of Health and Care Research (NIHR), UK.

Who is the main contact?
Dr Arit Inok, reactive@exeter.ac.uk</plainEnglishSummary>

      <inclusion>1. Participant is willing and able to give informed consent for participation in the study.
2. Male or Female, aged 65 years or above.
3. Access to a computer, tablet or smartphone, and access to the internet
4. Registered with a GP practice in England
5. Current diagnosis of MCI OR Subjective concerns regarding their cognitive function, based on completion of the IQCODE  questionnaire at screening. Participants with a score of 3.0 or above will be included if they fulfil at least two risk factors (below), or if they have a score of 3.17 or above.
6. Two or more of the following evidence-based risk factors for MCI and dementia:
6.1.	A first-degree family member with a history of dementia   (onset under 75 years old)
6.2.	One or more of: depression, diabetes, history of hypertension/cardiovascular disease / stroke, MCI
6.3.	Current smoker
6.4.	BMI > 30</inclusion>

	<description>Study Design: This project will deliver a 30-month single-arm clinical investigation of a cognitive monitoring app/website in 954 adults over 65 who are at risk of dementia. It seeks to establish the utility, acceptability and performance of the app as part of its route to regulatory approval as a Class Ils medical device.

Setting: Participants will take part from home on a device connected to the internet through an app downloaded from the app store or through a website. The app and websites use a validated digital infrastructure developed at the University of Exeter.

Target Population: Participants will be adults aged 65 with risk factors for dementia, including a sub-group of participants fulfilling criteria for Mild Cognitive Impairment.

Eligibility Criteria: Eligible participants will have either a diagnosis of MCI or have subjective cognitive impairment and at least two established risk factors for dementia. Participants will be aged 65 or above, have access to a computer or device connected to the internet and be residing in the UK. People will not be eligible if they have a visual or physical impairment that prevents them from completing computerised tests.

PARTICIPANT JOURNEY
1. Pre-screening & Recruitment: Participants will be recruited through primary care and memory clinics and through the PROTECT-UK ageing research cohort. Medical or research records will be pre-screened for Mild Cognitive Impairment and eligibility criteria. Participants will be signposted to the REACTIVE website and app to register for the trial.

2. Registration: Participants will register on REACTIVE. This will involve providing identifying information including their name, date of birth, address, email address, mobile telephone number and NHS number. They will also complete a demographics questionnaire to capture their sex, gender, ethnicity, educational attainment level and employment status.

3. Eligibility Assessment and Consent: Participants will complete a screening questionnaire to confirm eligibility. They will be presented with the Participant Information Sheet and will provide consent using an established digital consent system. They will nominate their GP surgery and will have the option of nominating a study partner who will complete questionnaires about them during the study.

4. Baseline Cognitive Assessment: Following consent participants will navigate to their study dashboard where they will follow a prescribed scheduled assessment process for the baseline timepoint. This will include a series of eight computerised cognitive tests to measure their memory, reaction time and problem-solving. They will first complete a five-minute practice session to familiarise them with the test system, followed by a 30-40 minute test session.

5. Baseline eligibility check: Participants will be shown a brief holding page while their cognitive test data is checked to ensure they do not have likely dementia at the beginning of the study. If their data does not fulfil criteria for dementia they will continue to complete their next assessments. If their data indicates a likely dementia then they will be contacted by a trained study team member and further assessments will be recommended with their GP.

6. Baseline questionnaire set: Participants will complete the following questionnaires at baseline:
6.1. Medical History Questionnaire: Report of existing medical conditions and current prescriptions through a tick-box selection process. Including weight, height, hearing loss and head injury.
6.2. Lifestyle Questionnaire: Participants will report key lifestyle factors that are linked to dementia risk use tick-box selection.
6.3. Function: Participants will complete the Amsterdam Instrumental Activities of Daily Living Scale
6.4. Subjective Cognitive Performance: Participants will complete the Questionnaire on Cognitive Decline in the Elderly (IQCODE), a self-rated measure of cognition.
6.5. Mental Health Questionnaire: Participants will complete the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) measure of depression, General Anxiety disorder (GAD-7) scale of anxiety, UCLA loneliness scale (UCLA) and Mild Behaviour Impairment scale.
6.6. Wellbeing: Participants will complete the EQ5D Quality of Life Questionnaire
6.7. Service Use: Participants will complete the Client Service Receipt Inventory to report use of services like GP surgeries and hospital appointments.

7. Blood and Saliva Sampling: Participants will receive two biofluid test kits through the post. This will contain one finger-prick blood sampling kit and one saliva collection tube. They will complete these tests by following the instructions provided and will return them in the post using a pre-addressed envelope. They will then enter an activation code into the REACTIVE app/website to confirm they have completed this step. This will then open the remaining study to them on the app/website.

8. Follow-up assessments: Participants will receive notifications and reminders to complete the cognitive and questionnaire assessments every six months.

9. Brain training games: During follow-up participants will have access to an evidence-based cognitive training programme on the app/website and will receive regular communications including advice on reducing risk of dementia.

10. Flagging and feedback on cognitive performance: After each time point, participants will receive feedback on their cognitive performance. This will involve being informed about their strongest cognitive domain at that testing session. If a drop in performance is detected that meets criteria for likely dementia the participant will be informed after quality checks have been performed. They will be invited to book a further assessment and their GP will be informed.

11. Clinical Dementia Rating Assessment and feedback: Participants will attend a video-based assessment with a study nurse. They will be asked to nominate a study partner who will attend this session with them. The session will involved completing a Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) assessment that includes answering questions and having a conversation about their brain health to enable the nurse to evaluate their cognition. If the nurse deems that the person does have likely dementia they will explain this to the participant and advise them to make an appointment with their GP to ensure they continue to a full referral and assessment. If they do not deem them to have dementia then the person will be informed and reassured. For either outcome, participants will be encouraged to continue completing assessments in the REACTIVE app.

12. GP Feedback: For all participants who are flagged with likely dementia, their GP will be informed about the flag and about the outcome of the Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) assessment. They will receive a report containing data from the person's cognitive assessments with guidance on interpretation. For people with a confirmed likely dementia the GP practice will be contacted to request medical record for the duration of the study.

13. End of Study: At the end of the study participants will be informed and thanked for their involvement. nent. They will be given the option to join the PROTECT-UK research cohort to continue to monitor their cognitive health and they will receive a report and summary of the research findings.

STUDY PARTNER JOURNEY
1. Recruitment, registration and consent: If a person is nominated as a study partner they will receive an email inviting them to take part. They will be signposted to the REACTIVE app/Website to register. They will be shown the Study Partner Information Sheet and will provide consent in the way described above.

2. Assessments: At baseline and every six months study partners will be asked to complete two questionnaires to answer questions about the participant. These are:

a. Cognitive Decline: Completion of the informant IQCODE to answer questions about the person's cognitive abilities and any change

b. Mild Behaviour Scale: Answering questions about the person's behaviour and how this may have changed.

3. Flagging process: If a participant is flagged with likely dementia the study partners would be invited to attend a video call assessment with the person and a study nurse. This would involve answering questions about the person and their behaviour.

4. End of Study: Study partners will be informed when the study ends and will receive a report and summary of the findings.</description>

      <ipdSharingStatement>The datasets generated and/or analysed during the current study will be available from the Chief Investigator upon reasonable request submitted by email to reactive@exeter.ac.uk. The data available for sharing will include anonymised participant-level data underlying the results reported in publications arising from the study, together with supporting study documentation where appropriate (e.g., data dictionary and statistical analysis plan). Data will become available following publication of the primary study results and will remain available for a minimum of 10 years thereafter, in accordance with institutional data retention policies.

Requests for access will be considered from bona fide researchers for scientifically and ethically sound research purposes. Applications must include a research proposal, evidence of appropriate ethical approval (where required), and a data management plan. Data sharing may be subject to a data sharing agreement.

Participants provided informed consent for the collection and use of their data for research purposes. All shared datasets will be anonymised prior to release to minimise the risk of participant identification. Access may be restricted where there are ethical, legal, regulatory, or confidentiality considerations that could compromise participant privacy or breach applicable data protection legislation, including the UK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) and Data Protection Act 2018.
